feed.title: NPR Topics: Business
feed.subtitle: Reporting on the money that flows through our economy, from Wall Street financial firms to Silicon Valley tech giants, small businesses, consumers, employers and workers. Plus podcast episodes of Planet Money and The Indicator.

entry.title: First-time homebuyers remain scarce, but a record share of them pay all cash
entry.summary: A new report finds generational wealth is widening the divide between homebuyers and those priced out. The median age of first-time buyers also remains at a record high.

entry.title: As budgets tighten, people are breaking out their library cards
entry.summary: Some Americans squeezed by high prices are relying more on their local libraries for things like books, streaming services and high-priced items like musical instruments and sewing machines.

entry.title: Does the blue wave mean lower gasoline and diesel prices soon? Don't hold your breath
entry.summary: A new Democratic majority in Congress could pressure the president to end the war in Iran. But it will be harder for them to directly affect fuel prices, which are tied to a complex international oil market.

entry.title: Legendary photographer on getting that perfect election night picture
entry.summary: On election night, photographers will be in position, ready to snap history-making moments. It's something Pulitzer-prize-winner photographer David Hume Kennerly, has done for decades.

entry.title: A Binance engineer thought he was interviewing for a job. Then the hackers pounced
entry.summary: North Korean hackers pulled off the biggest cyber heist ever by duping a Binance engineer into thinking he was being recruited for a job, the crypto exchange says.

entry.title: Eastern Kentucky welcomes data centers in hopes they make up for coal losses
entry.summary: In Kentucky's former coal country, data centers are a welcome sight as people hope they will bring in money.

entry.title: Chicago entrepreneur turns empty downtown office space into vertical gardens
entry.summary: The pandemic changed how and where the world works, leaving behind a lot of empty office space. One entrepreneur is starting to plant the seeds of a partial solution.

entry.title: When caring for aging family members becomes cost prohibitive
entry.summary: AARP reports family caregivers are spending 60% more than they were five years ago. Journalist Paula Span discusses the rising costs of caregiving and senior living, and the options available to us.

entry.title: Two economists studied California's billionaire tax. They reached wildly different conclusions
entry.summary: What happens in California could shape how America taxes the superrich. But will its billionaire tax fill state coffers — or drain them?

entry.title: 'Grasping at straws': Judge dismisses Trump suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
entry.summary: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.
